title: Close a jaw coupling on a gear reducer drive: turn the loose hub until its jaws find the spider, slide it to the gap
instruction: Close the jaw coupling between the gear reducer and the driven shaft.
context: Close a jaw coupling to the maker's hub gap G on a reducer drive. Industrial machinery mechanics and general maintenance workers couple drives back together after a motor, reducer or pump is swapped. O*NET lists "Reassemble equipment after completion of inspections, testing, or repairs." as a Core task of Industrial Machinery Mechanics (49-9041.00) and "Align and balance new equipment after installation." as a Core task of Maintenance and Repair Workers, General (49-9071.00). BLS OEWS (May 2025) counts 1,529,700 general maintenance and repair workers and 439,640 industrial machinery mechanics. The loose hub's jaws stop on the spider's legs until the hub is turned so they line up with the free pockets; the hub is then slid in until the gap between the hub faces is the maker's 'G'.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the station table top. Base plate: 1/2 in (1.27 cm) steel, x 25 to 61, y -26 to 20. The shafts' axis runs along y at x 33.0, 7.77 cm above the table (6.5 cm above the plate). Reducer: a right-angle worm gear reducer (gear case 11 x 11 cm, y 6.7 to 17.7) with its motor (12 cm across, 16 cm long) along +x, its 1 in output shaft pointing to the robot's right. Coupling: a Lovejoy L-100 L-type jaw coupling: two sintered-iron hubs (2.54 in / 64.5 mm across, 1.38 in / 35.05 mm length through bore, 2.09 in / 53.09 mm hub length, so the three jaws stand 18.03 mm out; 1.40 lb / 0.64 kg each), both bored 1 in with a 0.25 x 0.125 in keyway (the hub page's 'Dimension G', 0.71 in, is this jaw length, not the installation gap), and an L/AL099/100 SOX NBR solid-center spider (0.06 lb / 27 g, six legs; catalogue: 2.540 in / 64.5 mm across, 0.61 in / 15.5 mm wide, legs 0.43 in / 10.9 mm wide, solid center 1.030 in / 26.16 mm). The rigid sim spider is sized differently, as a stand-in for the snug rubber legs: 61 mm across, 18-degree legs (3 degrees of play a side for the rubber's squeeze), legs 18.29 mm long so the closed coupling has the published 3.480 in overall length, and a full-length 34.4 mm solid center, 0.3 mm a side inside the jaws, that rides on the jaws' inner faces to keep the spider centered as the snug real legs do. Each jaw is 36 degrees wide (estimated from maker photos; the hub page gives no jaw width). The reducer hub is clocked with a jaw straight down, a fixed start orientation for repeatable trials, so the rigid spider rests centered on it. The reducer hub is fixed flush with its shaft end, its jaw face at y 2.0, with the spider pushed onto its jaws. The driven shaft (1 in steel, y -24.0 to -0.06) turns freely in two pillow-block bearings (at y -11.5 and -20.5); the driven hub slides on it and turns with it (keyed slip fit). The driven hub starts with its face 45 mm from the reducer hub's face and its shaft turned so that each of its jaws stands square on a spider leg (30 degrees from the nearest phase that meshes). Arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. Real-world build: a fixed 1 in shaft in a block can stand in for the reducer side; the coupling, driven shaft and pillow blocks are the real parts.
scoring: 1.0: the driven hub in phase and slid in until the gap between the hub faces is Lovejoy's G for the L-100, 0.750 in (19.05 mm), within its allowed change of 0.040 in (18.03 to 20.07 mm), with the spider still seated on the reducer hub, every arm link at least 5 mm from the driven hub, the driven shaft and the spider, and everything still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 degrees a step) for 1 s. In phase means the driven hub's jaws within 6 degrees of the middle of the spider's free pockets (the play is 3 degrees a side). Seated means the spider's reducer-side end within 1.5 mm of the reducer hub's face, its axis within 1.5 mm and 4 degrees of the shafts' axis, and its legs within 5 degrees of their places either side of the reducer hub's jaws. 0.5: in phase with the jaws at least 5 mm into the spider's pockets, hands clear and still for 1 s, but the gap outside 18.03 to 20.07 mm. 0.25: in phase with the jaws 1 to 5 mm into the pockets, hands clear and still for 1 s. 0: anything else: a state still moving or not yet held for 1 s, doing nothing (the start scores 0), the jaws pushed onto the spider's legs out of phase, any hand still on the driven hub, the driven shaft or the spider at the end, the spider not seated, the hub closed without the spider, a face gap under 17.49 mm (driven into the spider), or the spider knocked off at any moment (its center 15 mm below the axis with no hand on it; latched). The score is the end state's. In simulation every condition is read from the parts' poses and per-hull arm-link distances. Real trial: the gap is checked with a 0.750 in gauge block or calipers after the hands are off. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide the driven hub back to its 45 mm mark, turn the driven shaft until a hub jaw lines up with a spider leg, and check that the spider is pushed onto the reducer hub's jaws. Under a minute. In simulation the reset is exact.
fidelity: Hub sizes, overall length, gap and tolerance from the maker; spider OD, width and center sized for the rigid model (catalogue sizes in setup). Rigid bodies, real contact, convex-hull jaws and legs. The rigid NBR spider has 3 degrees of play a side for its squeeze. Fixed box/cylinder reducer, motor, blocks. No set screws or keys; slip fit and bearings: light drag; shaft stops at +-180 deg. Friction: iron on steel 0.4/0.23 (cast-iron value), NBR 0.8/0.7 (Engineering ToolBox).
